Today is my first day in this English class.
Our classroom is on the first floor and it is very bright.
I sit on a chair near the window.
My blue book and my pen are on the table.
Our teacher is kind and she speaks slowly.
When I don't understand a word, I say excuse me and ask for help.
I am happy to learn with my new friends here.
There is a small cafe near my home.
I go there with my friend Lan in the morning.
The weather is hot today, so I want cold water.
Lan likes hot coffee with a little milk.
She says please and orders one cup of coffee.
We also buy fresh bread for breakfast.
We sit at a clean table by the door.
Before we leave, we say thank you to the staff.
I come home from work at six in the evening.
I put my bag and my phone on the small table.
My mother cooks warm rice and soup in the kitchen.
My family eats dinner together at seven.
After dinner, I drink a cup of warm tea.
Then I read my English book in my quiet room.
I write five new words in my notebook.
I feel tired at ten thirty, so I go to bed and sleep well.
Nam wakes up early every weekday morning.
He drinks a glass of warm water before breakfast.
After breakfast, he checks his bag and takes his bus card.
The bus stop is only five minutes from his street.
He waits near a small coffee shop on the left.
When the number seven bus arrives, Nam gets on and finds a seat by the window.
During the ride, he listens to a short English lesson on his phone.
He gets off near his office at eight thirty and starts his workday.
Every weekend, Mai walks to the local market near her house.
She likes going early in the morning because the food is very fresh.
First, she stops at a fruit stall and looks at the red apples.
She asks the seller how much a bag of apples costs.
The price is cheap, so she buys one bag for her family.
At the small fruit stall, she pays in cash.
Next, she visits a bakery next to the market gate to buy bread and milk.
At the bakery counter, she can easily pay by card.
On Friday afternoon, Tuan sends a message to his classmate Hoa.
He asks if she is free for lunch tomorrow.
Hoa replies that she would like to meet after her morning class.
There is a new noodle restaurant on Tran Phu Street.
Hoa asks where the restaurant is and what time they should meet.
Tuan explains that it is on the right, just two minutes from the train station.
He sends her a map on his phone so she can find it easily.
They agree to meet at twelve o'clock and have a great weekend meal.
Linh had an appointment with her dentist at three o'clock on Thursday afternoon.
However, her manager asked her to join an urgent project meeting at the same time.
During her lunch break, Linh called the clinic to check if another time was available.
The receptionist checked the schedule and offered two slots on Friday morning.
Nine thirty was convenient for Linh because her office was near the clinic.
She confirmed the new time and thanked the receptionist for her help.
Right after the call, she updated her digital calendar so she would not forget.
Preparing early allowed Linh to focus completely on her afternoon presentation.
Next month, Duc and his colleagues are going to travel to Da Nang for a conference.
They met this morning to compare two travel options and make a plan.
Flying is faster than taking the train, so it saves several hours.
However, the airport is far from the city center, and flight tickets are more expensive.
The overnight train is cheaper and has comfortable sleeping seats.
Also, the train station is very close to their hotel in Da Nang.
Duc suggested taking the morning flight out and returning by overnight train.
Everyone agreed that this choice gave them enough time for work and rest.
Last Saturday, Hanh planned a short weekend journey to Ninh Binh.
She got ready early and arrived at the station thirty minutes before departure.
Suddenly, heavy rain started, and the board showed a forty-minute delay.
Hanh had booked a local tour for ten o'clock, so she needed to inform the guide.
She called the tour office and explained the train delay clearly.
The staff was very helpful and changed her booking to the afternoon group at no extra charge.
While waiting at the station, Hanh drank warm tea and practiced her English flashcards.
Even with the delay, staying calm turned a difficult morning into a good travel experience.
Working with colleagues across different time zones requires thoughtful planning and clear written notes.
When a team in Hanoi collaborates with partners in London, their shared working hours are limited.
Instead of waiting for a live call, experienced engineers summarize the problem, context, and proposed solution in one message.
If a requirement is unclear, they do not hesitate to ask specific questions before writing code.
At the end of each day, a brief handover update helps the next shift continue without delay.
Although asynchronous communication takes effort at first, it reduces misunderstandings across the team.
Team members can also keep track of decisions and deadlines in one shared document.
As a result, this reliable habit builds lasting trust across the entire organization.
Online tools make studying and working more flexible, but looking at a screen all evening can hurt your sleep.
Last month, Quang realized that checking his phone late at night was a bad habit.
Whenever he stayed up late scrolling, he felt tired the next morning and could not focus.
He decided to make a simple change to deal with this problem.
Now, he charges his phone in the living room instead of keeping it beside his bed.
Before going to sleep, he spends twenty minutes reading a printed book or reviewing calm notes.
In my opinion, setting a clear boundary with technology is an effective strategy for mental energy.
After three weeks, Quang noticed that his memory and morning concentration had improved significantly.
For a long time, plastic waste and parked motorbikes were a frustrating issue in our neighborhood.
Narrow sidewalks made walking unsafe for children and older residents.
Last month, the community organized a weekend meeting to discuss practical alternatives.
Some residents complained about the noise, while others pointed out the lack of recycling bins.
After weighing the pros and cons, everyone agreed on a three-step action plan.
Clear parking lines were painted, and new sorting bins were placed near every corner.
Over fifty families participated in the Sunday clean-up to reduce street litter.
The experience taught us an important lesson: small shared efforts can transform our living environment.
